content.text:
**Finding: compliant (at fallback)** — Rule T4C, Termination for convenience.

- **Our exit right:** § 17(b) lets Sparkling terminate at any time on 90 days' written notice — within the fallback range (60–90 days), with no early-termination fee or penalty anywhere in the agreement (§ 11 / Fee Schedule impose none), which is better than the fallback's 3-month fee cap.
- **Vendor exit right:** Garman has no convenience right at all; its only termination triggers are insolvency events and uncured material default under § 17(c), meeting the preferred position.
- **Noted, not flagged:** notice sits at the outer edge of the fallback (90 vs. preferred 30 days), and § 17(b) has no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (refunds for services not yet rendered appear only on termination for Garman's default, p0128). These are sub-elements to raise if the agreement is reopened, not standalone deviations.

No redline proposed.
